alpha.formation_name: Forward Destroyer Wall with Flanking Reserve
alpha.selection_rationale: Committing fully to a fast-hull doctrine (all ships 2-3g) so the whole fleet can dictate range against any slower capital-heavy enemy fleet, deny them closing speed for both their guns and any torpedoes, and choose engagement windows. Four destroyers form the main gunline (spinal coiler + coilgun each, solid nose armor), two frigates add cheap coilgun/PD support, and two corvettes provide torpedo harassment and extra PD while sharing the same speed envelope so the formation never has to choose between abandoning slow capitals and eating enemy fire at capital speed.
alpha.formation_rationale: The four destroyers form a forward wall, staggered laterally and vertically (±10-15km z, ±20-60km y) to absorb the first exchange while complicating enemy spinal-weapon targeting solutions - a shooter can't line up more than one hull at a time. The two frigates sit just behind and inboard of the destroyer line, close enough (within ~60-100km) to overlap point-defense coverage against incoming torpedo salvos aimed at the vanguard. The two corvettes are held well back (-40km) and pushed wide (±90km y) out of immediate gun range, positioning them to swing around the flanks once the main lines engage, or to peel off and harass unsupported enemy elements without being caught in the initial exchange.

beta.selection_rationale: A homogenous fast gun line: six destroyers at 2g outrun torpedo cruisers and slow capitals, can burn away from incoming saturation so torpedo NEZs go dry, then close inside 300 km and crack thin flank/tail armor with spinal 4.3 GJ hits. One hull class keeps the AI execution uniform and simple.
beta.formation_rationale: Compact staggered wall keeps all ships within ~100 km so point-defense batteries overlap against torpedo salvos, while lateral offsets complicate enemy spinal-geometry targeting. A forward vanguard pair absorbs the first gun exchange, and a rear pair holds as reserve/PD anchors.
